DESCRIPTION: InformationSelonsertib (GS-4997) Selonsertib (GS-4997) is a highly selective and potent once-daily oral ASK1 inhibitor with potential anti-inflammatory, antineoplastic and anti-fibrotic activities.TargetsASK1 (Cell-free assay) 8.3(pIC50)In vivoAn orally bioavailable inhibitor of apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1), with potential anti-inflammatory, antineoplastic and anti-fibrotic activities. Upon oral administration, ASK1 inhibitor GS-4997 targets and binds to the catalytic kinase domain of ASK1 in an ATP-competitive manner, thereby preventing its phosphorylation and activation. DESCRIPTION: InformationSelonsertib (GS-4997) Selonsertib (GS-4997) is a highly selective and potent once-daily oral ASK1 inhibitor with potential anti-inflammatory, antineoplastic and anti-fibrotic activities.TargetsASK1 (Cell-free assay) 8.3(pIC50)In vivoAn orally bioavailable inhibitor of apoptosis signal-regulating kinase 1 (ASK1), with potential anti-inflammatory, antineoplastic and anti-fibrotic activities. Upon oral administration, ASK1 inhibitor GS-4997 targets and binds to the catalytic kinase domain of ASK1 in an ATP-competitive manner, thereby preventing its phosphorylation and activation. This prevents the phosphorylation of downstream kinases, such as c-Jun N-terminal kinases (JNKs) and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK). By preventing the activation of ASK1-dependent signal transduction pathways, GS-4997 prevents the production of inflammatory cytokines, down-regulates the expression of genes involved in fibrosis, suppresses excessive apoptosis and inhibits cellular proliferation. DESCRIPTION:
USP Textiles:
Antimicrobial Effectiveness Test (AET) 
Preservatives are commonly added to nonsterile dosage forms of drugs to prevent microbial contamination in drug formulation. Drugs can get contaminated with microorganisms inadvertently during manufacturing process or during the continual use of a product.
The USP  antimicrobial effectiveness test or the preservative efficacy test determines if a preservative is appropriate and effective for a product formulation. AET is performed as part of a stability study to ensure if the preservative system is effective against microbial growth up till the expiration date of a product. 
AET is performed by inoculating the product with a recommended level of 5 microorganisms. The microorganism panel includes 3 bacteria - Escherichia coli , Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus; 1 fungi - Aspergillus brasiliensis and 1 yeast - Candida albicans. AET evaluates the effectiveness of the preservative by comparing the microorganism levels over a period of 28 days with the initial microorganim levels, and the preservative effectiveness is determined based USP guidelines.
